summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: "A Little Irish Girl" (J. M. Callwell, 1920s; Blackie & Son)

### Characters
- **Norah O'Brien** (11, youngest; short, dark, shaggy black hair, turned-up nose, wide mouth, dark-blue "Irish eyes"; loves Irish name, spells without final h; quick, mischievous; father Piers died ~6 months before; wears shabby black mourning frock)
- **Anstace O'Brien** (elder sister, ~19-20; named after godmother Cousin Ansey; gentle, practical, became governess; later nurses Norah)
- **Roderick O'Brien** (eldest, tall, dark-haired; ex-college honours; was to go to bar; now lawyer's clerk, cough/weak lungs; writer for magazines; later engaged to Ella)
- **Manus O'Brien** (12, close to Norah; at cheap school in Kent, Dr. Ford's school; sunburnt, squat; later Harrow planned)
- **Piers O'Brien** (father; Irish journalist; died in Hampstead after chill)
- **Marion Belthorpe** (mother, English; eloped with Piers, jilting Nicholas O'Brien; died early, "beyond Norah's memory")
- **Miss Euphemia Clarkson** (youngest of three Miss Clarksons; teaches juniors; strict; kind-hearted); **Miss Clarkson** (eldest, stately, head of Treherne House); **Miss Susan** (second sister)
- **Fräulein Glock** (German governess)
- **Lily Allardyce** (Norah's friend; pink-and-white, rich; parents from Hampshire/Heron's Court; going to Paris for Easter)
- **Louisa Flabby, Constance Lane** (geography class girls)
- **Cousin Ansey (Anstace O'Brien)** (d. last week; engaged to Hugh Masters who never returned; mad; asylum in Dublin 12 years; left Kilshane to Piers's children)
- **Uncle Nicholas O'Brien** (Moyross Abbey; old, grey-haired, proud, hates Piers; copper mine on Drinane Head; prudent)
- **Harry Wyndham** (grandnephew, son of Nicholas's niece; sent to Austria/"Carpathian Mountains"/Jarmany training; wants army)
- **Ella Wyndham** (Nicholas's great-niece, gentle, fair; pony Sheila; later marries Roderick)
- **Miss Browne ("Brownie")** (governess to Wyndhams, India; prim; wears glasses; bonnet on backwards)
- **Mr. Lynch** (old rector; Mrs. Lynch; Piers's old tutor/boxed ears)
- **Biddy Hogan**, **Tom Hogan** (her brother, ex-coachman, now steward), **Lanty Hogan** (red-headed, 7 orphans), **Bride** (Lanty's sister, maid), **Kat** (2-yr-old)
- **Connor** (car driver), **Mrs. Connor** & **Thady** (potato scones, pigs)
- **M'Bain** (Scotch manager of mine); **Malachy Flanagan** (red-bearded steersman, orator; mother old woman)
- **Captain Lester, R.M.** (resident magistrate; sandy-haired, jolly)
- **Lady Louisa Butler** (Dromore; Irish brogue)
- **Cartwright** (butler at Moyross), **Dr. Hanlon** (doctor), **Cousin Ansey's pearls**

### Places
Treherne House (N. London, Miss Clarksons' school; Hampstead Heath home earlier); Kilshane (small house on cliffs near Moyross, Clare; ~2 miles from Moyross); Moyross Abbey (Nicholas's; Monks' Walk; cove; abbey window); Ballyfin (railway terminus, 12 Irish miles); Ballintaggart Cave (seals); Portkerin (cove); Drinane Head (still on promontory, tarn, hovel); Dromore (Lady Louisa's, 14 miles); Ennis jail; Euston station; Dublin.

### Chronology / Events
1. Ch I: Geography lesson at Treherne House (Turkey in Asia); Norah daydreams ("Tuesday fortnight"); sent to bottom; Lily consoles; Norah's family background; Lily going to Paris; Norah's holidays alone.
2. Ch II: Anstace visits Norah; Cousin Ansey's legacy: small property Kilshane (~£100/yr); Roderick visited Moyross funeral; Uncle Nicholas's feud explained (Marion jilted him, married Piers); Harry Wyndham to inherit; Norah protests.
3. Ch III: Norah's freak: tea-tray toboggan with Lily down staircase; Miss Clarkson kisses Norah; Lily's pincushion (sunflower).
4. Ch IV: Term ends; Norah leaves; sea-crossing to Dublin; train to Ballyfin; outside car, Connor; arrive Kilshane at night; Biddy and Tom greet.
5. Ch V: Kilshane morning; kitchen filthy (hens, cat, turkey, one-eyed collie licking pan); Biddy hurls candlestick; Miss Ansey's room, china broken by hens; Tom Hogan; Biddy leaves; Lanty and Bride.
6. Ch VI: Mr. Lynch's report of mine strike, M'Bain; Manus arrives (diphtheria at school); Norah collects him at Ballyfin with Connor; Mrs. Connor's potato scones; Ella's pony Sheila runs away; Roderick catches it at gate; Ella taken to Kilshane; Miss Browne arrives; "Brownie" bonnet mishap.
7. Ch VII: Miss Browne's backstory (Dinapore, cholera, Mrs. Wyndham); Ella and Mr. Nicholas (portrait of Marion); Nicholas's reaction.
8. Ch VIII: Ballintaggart Cave: Manus and Lanty plan seal hunt; Norah eavesdrops via dairy window; Norah rows; seal kills; Manus rescued by Lanty's club; Norah's fears; "Bedad" remark.
9. Ch IX: Row home; steersman hails boat; Lanty goes to Drinane Head; Monks' Walk "ghost" (white figure with raised arm); Manus fires at table-cloth; Miss Browne scolds laundry maid (Bride's sister? laundry girl) over ruined damask; children hide; Manus's Lanty secret.
10. Ch X: Table-cloth gossip; Mr. O'Brien closes mine, dismisses men; Lady Louisa invitation; Biddy and dress; Captain Lester's note (raid on still); Bride's dinner blunders; Manus tells Norah of still on Drinane Head.
11. Ch XI: Norah wakes at 2:30/3:00 (clock); Manus refuses to go; Norah walks alone to Drinane Head at dawn; warns Malachy and Lanty; Malachy hides her with shawl as "his little girl"; Malachy's mother.
12. Ch XII: Police search; Roderick and Captain Lester; hat not recognised; Captain Lester's warning speech; Malachy carries Norah home on back; Roderick sees her; Norah says she bought eggs. Breakfast: Lester's speech; Manus blames Norah.
13. Ch XIII: Evening: Norah and Manus visit mine (Roderick and Anstace at Dromore); Malachy harangues miners on trolly; crowd marches on Moyross; children run.
14. Ch XIV: Moyross: Harry Wyndham home (fled Austria); Ella, Miss Browne, Cartwright; children warn; Harry defends house; Norah takes candle and quilt; climbs abbey window, impersonates white nun ("St. Bridget"); crowd flees; Norah falls.
15. Ch XV: Norah unconscious; Mr. O'Brien (Nicholas) realizes Norah = Piers's child; Roderick and Anstace arrive; Anstace called "Marion" by Nicholas.
16. Ch XVI: Peace: Nicholas admits love for Marion; Harry to army; Malachy weeps; M'Bain and miners settle; Roderick to run mine; Roderick and Ella engaged; Norah wakes; Lanty promises no potheen; becomes under-keeper; Nicholas: Roderick heir; "a year next week since he died."

## BOOK 2: "The Templeton Case" (Victor L. Whitechurch; Edward J. Clode, 1924)

### Characters
- **Reginald Templeton** (murdered, ~25 yrs? actually ~50s; explorer, South Africa; yacht *Firefly*; cousin of Canon Fittleworth; left estate to Winifred Cotterill; had uncut diamonds, 32 total)
- **Tom Gale** (crew/cook of schooner *Lucy*; gossip; saw Templeton cross, Moss on shore; cigars)
- **Mrs. Yates** (widow, landlady of "Mariner's Arms," Marsh Quay)
- **Harold Grayson** (artist, lodger at Mariner's Arms; cycled away early Sunday; alias? Actually real name Grayson; son of Osmond Grayson, Marlow; lawsuit with Templeton; fiancé of Winnie)
- **Jim Webb** (crew of Firefly; from 31 Fore Street, Salcombe; employed by Jefferies; found body)
- **Mr. Joseph Proctor** (retired cigar merchant, bald, egg-shaped head, velveteen jacket, Switzerland photo (Julier Pass); cleared in end); great-nephew **Phil** (~15)
- **Superintendent Thomas Norton** (quiet, big black moustache)
- **Detective-Sergeant Bob Colson** (plain clothes, slight, shrewd grey eyes; wife unnamed, "Mrs. Colson")
- **Major Renshaw** (Chief Constable; military moustache)
- **Canon Charles Fittleworth** (cousin of Templeton; pince-nez; wife Mrs. Fittleworth; daughter Doris; Charles; Cathedral Close; Frattenbury)
- **Francis Norwood** (coroner & solicitor; hatchet face; never married; left-handed; murderer; suicide in cell)
- **Anthony Crosby** (lawyer, Crosby and Paxton, 17b Lincoln's Inn Fields; executor)
- **Isaac Moss** (Jewish diamond dealer, 13a Hatton Garden; house "Fairview," 53 Compton Avenue, Brondesbury; wife Mrs. Moss; housekeeper couple; crossed to yacht ~1 a.m.)
- **Constable Gadsden**, **Constable Drake**, **Peters**, **Tyler** (detective), **Joe Thatcher** (poacher)
- **Winifred "Winnie" Cotterill** (artist; real name Forbes; father Percy Forbes, embezzler, died Princetown; mother Mabel Cotterill)
- **Maude Wingrave** (friend, flatmate)
- **Sir James Perrivale** (big-game hunter; Ezra Grice rescued)
- **Ezra Grice** (former clerk of Norwood; survived in South Africa)
- **Dr. Hazell** (doctor; "Virginian Reefs" shares), **Sir Peter Birchnall**, **Rev. Alfred Carringford**, **Stephen Merrifield** (corn merchant), **Mr. Buckland** (chemist), **Dean**
- **George Simmonds** (cottager)

### Places
Marsh Quay (estuary, Frattenbury 2 miles N); Mariner's Arms; Frattenbury (Cathedral, Close, Dolphin hotel, Wheatsheaf at Selham, Chester hotel London); Linderton; Selham; Battersea (flat); Hatton Garden; Princetown; Ennis (not here).

### Events (Book 2)
1. Ch I: Tom Gale on Lucy; yacht *Firefly* arrives; Templeton (cigar; band thrown in grate); Grayson in bar parlour; Webb's chat.
2. Ch II: Templeton rows across to Moss's house; Grayson watches; Tom points out Moss; Templeton returns; night.
3. Ch III: Webb finds body Sunday morning; Mrs. Yates; Proctor; Phil sent to Frattenbury; police (Norton, doctor, Colson) investigate; Webb's letter to Fittleworth; Moss's address; Norton visits coroner.
4. Ch IV: Canon Fittleworth finds cigar band on floor; keeps it; Norwood (coroner) schedules inquest; Moss's house visit (Mrs. Moss gone to London); housekeeper.
5. Ch V: Colson at Mariner's Arms; description of Grayson; footprints/ferrule evidence; Canon's walking stick; letter from Crosby; blotter fragments ("...Y rs f ithfully R. Templeton"); diamond bag; Peters sent to canoe; walking stick with chipped handle found in dinghy.
6. Ch VI: Colson copies stick at Blake's tobacconist; wife discusses; night watch; dummy stick placed; Proctor's canoe found.
7. Ch VII: Inquest (Mon); Webb, doctor (dagger, triangular wound), Tom Gale, Canon produces cigar band; jury passes band; band swapped; adjourned to Saturday week.
8. Ch VIII: Winnie Cotterill (Battersea) reads report; visits Frattenbury; Crosby and Canon; Templeton's will leaves her all; Canon's wife; Grayson name mentioned; Winnie faints/distressed.
9. Ch IX: Tom Gale gives cigar; Colson's deductions; Grayson detained; Moss identified.
10. Ch X: Grayson detained at Linderton (Constable Drake; Mrs. Goring); Major Renshaw questions; Crosby on lawsuit; blotter copy "Ezra's ices".
11. Ch XI: Funeral; Winnie's déjà vu; Canon's letter from Norton; cigar band comparison; band found different; Canon's cigar box; Colson rides Canon's motorcycle; Mrs. Yates alibi; Grayson freed; dinner with Canon.
12. Ch XII: Plan to plant false trail; Norwood's dinner party (Sir Peter, Dr. Hazell, Rev. Carringford); Thatcher poacher's statement (boat from other side, motorcar at 1 a.m.); Colson checks boat paint.
13. Ch XIII: Winnie & Grayson at station; Moss confesses; diamonds: 32, one missing; receipt; Moss's alibi at Chester hotel; Moss released; Colson: "Proctor, cigar merchant".
14. Ch XIV: Crosby & Winnie: inherits £2,000; Templeton's sealed letter reveals Winnie's father Forbes; Winnie engaged to Grayson; dinner at Petit Cygne.
15. Ch XV: Colson's reconstruction (A = murderer); Proctor's cigar cupboard; Colson steals cigar; cigar firm; Proctor's trap.
16. Ch XVI: Inquest re-opened; postman, Moss, Thatcher; jury verdict "wilful murder against person(s) unknown"; Proctor's alibi (played bridge with Merrifield until 1:00; Merrifield drove him home; left 1:30).
17. Ch XVII: Mrs. Colson's theories; left-handed man; Simmonds says Templeton carried stick by middle; Buckland; Norwood's law office; Dr. Hazell's losses; Canon's list; Dean had a cigar.
18. Ch XVIII: Crosby's letter; Sir James Perrivale reveals Grice; Norwood asks Colson about Grice.
19. Ch XIX: Crosby finds Forbes case; Virginian Reefs; Colson re-interviews Proctor (jurymen Bailey/Westall swap); Dean abroad; Grice arrives Plymouth; Colson's evidence against Norwood.
20. Ch XX: Canon's study confrontation; Colson accuses Norwood; stick; Ezra Grice produced; Norwood arrested.
21. Ch XXI: Grice's story; Norwood's suicide note (braces, cell); Crosby undecided about telling Winnie.

### Names/Key details
- Murder: stabbed in back, triangular dagger, through heart; Templeton ~ midnight/1 a.m. Sunday.
- Walking stick: Alpine square ferrule, chipped handle; dummy by Colson.
- Cigar brand: Canon's special Cuban brand from de Garcia (Spanish friend).
- Diamonds: 32 uncut; Moss held; receipt for stones.
- Norwood: left-handed; Ezra Grice clerk; embezzlement blackmail £10,000.
